transcript.content: Hello, I'm glad you're here. What brings you in to see me today?

Ever since the shooting ten days ago, I feel like I’m constantly on guard, checking every room and jumpy about anything happening around me. I was right there when a gunman started firing outside a bar, and my parents and HR finally urged me to come in because I'm just so on edge.
Along with feeling constantly on guard, have you been experiencing any unwanted memories, flashbacks, or nightmares about the shooting?
No, I haven't really been having nightmares or flashbacks about the shooting. It's more that I'm just constantly tense and on edge during the day.
Have you found yourself actively avoiding the area where the shooting happened, or trying to avoid thinking or talking about it?

Yes, absolutely. I'm completely avoiding crowded bars and popular nightlife spots now, even though that's how I usually network for my job. I actually had to skip a major evening client event last week because I just couldn't bring myself to face going back into that kind of environment.
Even though you haven't had nightmares or flashbacks, do you find sudden, unwanted thoughts or images of the shooting popping into your mind during the day?

No, I don't really get sudden thoughts or images of it popping up during the day. Honestly, the actual moment of the shooting feels more like a blank space or a fog in my head rather than something I keep picturing.
Since the shooting, have you felt emotionally numb, or detached and cut off from your family and friends?

Yes, I feel completely numb and disconnected lately. Even when my team closed a big deal this week and my dad tried to celebrate with me, I just felt totally flat and unable to feel any real happiness or warmth. It honestly feels like I'm just watching someone else's life instead of living my own.
When you are confronted with things that remind you of the shooting, do you experience physical reactions like a racing heart, sweating, or trouble breathing?

I haven't really noticed those specific physical reactions just from reminders, mainly because I've been actively avoiding bars and crowded places altogether. But my heart definitely slams in my chest and I start shaking when I'm startled by sudden loud noises, like a car backfiring or a dropped stapler at the office.
When you thought about attending that client event, or whenever you are confronted with reminders of the shooting, do you experience intense feelings of anxiety, fear, or distress?

Yes, I felt an overwhelming sense of anxiety and dread just thinking about it. I had to skip that client event because I simply couldn't face going back to a crowded bar, and even the thought of being in that kind of environment makes me feel incredibly tense and overwhelmed with fear.
Have you ever experienced these kinds of symptoms for more than a month in the past, or is this the first time you have felt this way?
No, I've never felt like this before in my life. This is the very first time I've experienced anything like this, and it all started exactly ten days ago right after the shooting.
Since the shooting, have you been having trouble falling or staying asleep, or have you noticed yourself feeling unusually irritable?
No, I haven't really noticed any trouble sleeping, and I wouldn't say I've been feeling unusually angry or irritable. It's more just that constant feeling of being on guard and jumpy during the day.
Even if you don't have clear visual memories, do you ever suddenly feel or act as if the shooting is actually happening all over again in that very moment?

No, I don't ever feel like I'm actually back in that exact moment reliving it. While I'm constantly terrified and on guard that something like that might happen again, I don't lose touch with reality or feel like the shooting is happening all over again in the present.
Have you had any difficulty concentrating on your work or other daily tasks since the shooting?

Yes, my brain has felt completely fogged out since the shooting. I'll be in the middle of a sales call or a simple email and completely lose my train of thought. I just end up staring at my screen because I can't seem to make basic decisions on what to do next.
Since the shooting, have you felt a constant sense of worry, or a feeling that you are unable to cope or plan for the future?

Yes, I feel this constant, exhausting tension because my body is always on edge, waiting for something terrible to happen again. It really feels like I can't cope with daily life anymore—I'm skipping social events, failing to handle my normal responsibilities, and I can't even make simple decisions at work like who I need to call next.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with significant emotional and behavioral symptoms (anxiety, hypervigilance, emotional numbing, avoidance, and cognitive difficulties) following a life-threatening traumatic stressor (a shooting) 10 days ago. The symptoms cause marked impairment in occupational and social functioning (skipping client events, inability to make decisions at work). The duration of 10 days is too long for an ICD-10 Acute Stress Reaction (F43.0), which typically subsides within hours or days, but is too short for PTSD (F43.1), which requires a duration of at least 1 month. Additionally, the patient lacks intrusive reliving symptoms (flashbacks or nightmares). Therefore, Adjustment Disorder (F43.2) is the most appropriate diagnosis.
